_comment: COUPLING tier-2. A SECOND cross-code pair for two-way TSI, so the capability belongs to the coupling path rather than to one pairing that happened to work: NGSolve thermal with FEniCSx structural, and scikit-fem thermal with NGSolve structural. NGSolve is the hard participant on purpose — netgen gives it an UNSTRUCTURED mesh while dolfinx and scikit-fem both use a tensor-product triangulation here, so every exchange in these arrangements maps between a regular grid and an irregular cloud, in both directions, and no node can coincide with a partner node by accident. It is also a different structural discretisation: VectorH1 order 2 with per-component Dirichlet boundaries (dirichletx= / dirichlety=), where a plain dirichlet= would clamp both components and silently turn transverse rollers into a built-in edge. Same battery as the other pair fixtures: convergence, monolithic agreement, interface sensitivity per participant, and the reverse-direction control checked both for size and against the monolithic two-way-minus-one-way difference.

_mutation.note: Kill the reverse direction. Both arrangements converge faster and every iteration-level check passes; the monolithic comparison and `reverse_direction_is_active` are what fail.

Export the volumetric strain from THIS participant's nodes but hand the partner the coordinates shifted by a quarter of the body. The interpolation then samples the strain field in the wrong place — a mesh-to-mesh mapping error, which is the failure mode a volume coupling on non-matching meshes has and an interface coupling does not. It converges: a wrong but consistent map still has a fixed point.

            "E_MOD": repr(p.e_mod)
